texts: good. the walk, the base as a part of the cliff, the morning and both date terms (day 1, Year 1) all land. One caveat no rewording fixes: 'day 1' occupies the slot a calendar day-of-month would, with no month to anchor it, so two of your dates will not automatically order against each other.

mixed: the sentence's own content is fully covered - a two-member group of assistants, the walking, 'with Tessa Brae' as a co-walker, and a per-member rule so each assistant's own walk is derivable. What is lost is the time: 'On day 1 of Year 1 ... in the morning' reaches only sentence 1's walk, and nothing carries a time frame forward across sentences, so this sentence and every later one in the episode ends up with no date. If the episode is meant to sit on that morning, give the sentences that need it their own anaphoric time phrase - e.g. 'That morning, two assistants walked with Tessa Brae.' - which copies day 1 and Year 1 onto the new event.

bad: 'had molted' says the molting came earlier than the rest of the episode, but the parse keeps only a plain past tense and records no ordering at all, so nothing places the molting before the walking or the collecting. Put the ordering in words rather than leaving it to the perfect: 'The three sky-cats had molted during the hunt, before that walk.' The rest is fine - the group of three, 'during the hunt', and a per-cat molting rule.

bad: two things go missing. 'had fallen' again yields only a past tense with no ordering, so nothing records that the feathers fell before Tessa Brae walked the cliff base and collected them; and, unlike the assistants and the sky-cats, this feather group gets no per-member rule, so nothing follows about any individual feather having fallen (that second one is a translator slip, not something your wording caused). For the ordering, name the anchor: 'Feathers had fallen to the base of the cliff before that walk.'
good. the partitive is right - forty-one feathers as a counted subset of the fallen feathers introduced in the previous sentence - and the collecting is placed at the same cliff base as sentence 1.

good. the weighing, the feathers as the same forty-one she collected, and the Watch as the place all land. Note only that 'the Watch' is recorded as an ordinary common noun with no name of its own (the default for a bare capitalized kind word), so downstream it is identified by kind and salience rather than by the name 'Watch'.
good. the recording, the feathers as the same set, and the ledger with the Watch as its holder are all there, with the ledger kept as where the recording happened.
good. the feather bin is typed and unpacked as a kind of bin, and the feathers land in it as the destination of the adding.
